evidence.curator_note: SUBSTRATE READ FROM THE DRAWING: the leftmost structure is MeOCO-CH=CH-C(=O)-O-CH3 in square brackets with '+.' outside the bracket, i.e. the molecular ion of dimethyl fumarate (the two ester groups are drawn on opposite sides of the C=C, the trans/E arrangement; C6H8O4, M+. 144.042). One ester is abbreviated 'MeOCO' and attached to the upper alkene carbon; the other is drawn out in full, and ONE hydrogen of its O-methyl is written explicitly and points back across at the alkene. THIS STEP: that explicit hydrogen migrates to the alkene carbon that carries the MeOCO group, through the six-membered ring H(-C(methyl)-O-C(=O)-C-C) - exactly the '6-membered-ring H-displacement' the running text on this page invokes. The result is the centre structure the book prints: MeOCO-CH2-C(+)H-C(=O)-O-CH2., an even-electron carbenium centre on the carbon alpha to the intact ester and the odd electron on the O-methylene, which the book marks with a dot. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 0 arc(s) for this step - the leftmost structure carries no curved arrows at all; the transfer is indicated only by the explicitly drawn hydrogen, the 'r H' label over the arrow, and the printed product. All three encoded moves are therefore curator-supplied to balance the electrons: move <1> the odd electron of the radical site to the forming C-H bond, move <2> one electron of the breaking C(methyl)-H bond to that same forming bond, move <3> the implicit homolysis hook that leaves the second electron of the C-H bond on the methylene carbon, which is what creates the radical the book prints as a dot. LOCALIZATION (convention C): the book leaves the charge and the odd electron DELOCALIZED - '+.' is printed outside the bracket and the C=C is drawn as an intact double bond. A mapped SMILES cannot carry that, so one resonance form is chosen and used consistently: the alkene pi bond is ionized as C(1).-C(2)+, i.e. a single C-C bond with the unpaired electron on the carbon that bears MeOCO and the positive charge on the carbon that bears the drawn-out ester. That is the only localization from which a homolytic H transfer reproduces the centre structure the book prints (the H must arrive at a radical site, and the '+' must end up where the book draws 'HC+'). STEREOCHEMISTRY: the drawn trans (fumarate) geometry is not encoded in the SMILES; it does not affect this intramolecular transfer, which reaches only to the neighbouring carbon. ATOM-MAP NOTE: the migrating hydrogen is written [1H:7] so RDKit keeps it explicit and it can carry an atom map; it is ordinary protium, not a label the book draws.

Equation 8.111, SECOND arrow, labelled 'rd'. The O-methylene radical of the distonic ion attacks the carbon that carries the MeOCO group and displaces that group as a radical: the book prints the products as 'MeOCO .' plus a five-membered ring drawn as HC(+) at the upper left, then a CH2, then a CH2, then the ring oxygen at the right, then the C=O at the bottom back to the HC(+). That is the gamma-butyrolactone ring carrying the charge on its alpha carbon (2-oxotetrahydrofuran-3-ylium, C4H5O2+), and 'MeOCO .' is the methoxycarbonyl radical .C(=O)OCH3 (59.013); 144 - 59 = 85 for the ion. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 2 arc(s), both single-barbed fishhooks, meeting barb-to-barb (they form the characteristic 'W' where the two heads touch) in the empty space between the radical-bearing methylene and the MeOCO-bearing carbon - i.e. on the forming C-C ring bond. Arc 1 starts on the bond joining the 'MeOCO' label to the 'H2C' carbon; arc 2 starts at the radical dot on the methylene. Moves <1,2> are those two drawn arcs; move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page) - it carries the second electron of the cleaving C-C(O)OMe bond onto the ester carbon, which is what actually makes the 'MeOCO .' radical the book writes as a product. LABEL READING: 'MeOCO-' is read as methoxycarbonyl, CH3-O-CO-, attached through the carbonyl CARBON; the mass balance (loss of 59, not 75) confirms it is the ester and not a carbonate.

NO MOD RULE IS CROSS-LINKED. rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no '8.111' key (its chapter-8 index runs 8.1-8.14 only, German-edition numbering). The candidates were CHECKED against this record's own species with RDKit, not assumed (convention E). (i) 'substituion' '[_A]1[C]2[C]3[_A+.]4>>[_A.]1.[C]2[C]3[_A+]4{-}2' is the generic ring-closing displacement and is conservation-clean, so it is live. Its left pattern '[*]-[#6]-[#6]-[*+]' DOES match the distonic intermediate exactly once, but the match is chemically wrong in two independent ways, so the rule is a mismatch and is listed in rule_mismatches. First, the matched atoms are O(map 10)-C(map 8)-C(map 1)-C(map 2): the rule would treat the CARBENIUM carbon (map 2) as the attacking centre, close a three-membered ring onto the ester carbon (map 8) and expel the methoxy oxygen (map 10) as a radical - nothing like the five-membered lactone and the .COOCH3 loss the book draws. Second, the rule's attacking atom is specified as '[_A+.]', charge AND unpaired electron on the same atom; an explicit atom-by-atom scan of the distonic intermediate finds NO such atom - the charge sits on carbon map 2 with no unpaired electron and the odd electron sits on carbon map 6 with no charge - so the pattern's decisive label is unsatisfiable here even though the plain connectivity matches. (ii) IMS_4_42_rd '[C]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[Cl+.]6>>[C.]1.[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[Cl+]6{-}2' is the closest ring-size analogue (it closes a five-membered ring and expels a carbon radical) but it requires a chlorine as the attacking site: 0 matches. (iii) No rule in the set performs an H transfer onto an ionized C=C, so step 1 has no candidate at all. Every chapter-4 'displacement reaction' rule (IMS_4_43_, IMS_4_44_ind/rH, IMS_4_45_*, IMS_4_46_*) is built on an amine, a chloroalkane or an ester with the reacting hydrogen on the O-alkyl chain, none of which is this substrate.

NO MEASUREMENT ON THE PAGE (convention F): equation 8.111 prints no m/z and no intensity anywhere - the products are drawn as structures only ('MeOCO .' and the lactone ring), and the surrounding prose quotes no abundance for this reaction. Every species is therefore detected=false, the single peak assignment has status 'inferred' and relative_intensity is omitted. observed_mz 85.0284 is the curator-computed monoisotopic mass of the C4H5O2+ lactone cation (RDKit ExactMolWt, electron-mass corrected), and ms_context.precursor_mz 144.0417 is likewise the computed M+. of dimethyl fumarate C6H8O4 for the structure read off the drawing; the page states neither number, nor an electron energy - the 70 eV EI setting follows the book's default EI convention, not a statement on this page.
